definitions.gloss: Girls' Day festival; Peach Festival; Doll Festival
definitions.explanation: A traditional festival on March 3rd celebrating the health and happiness of girls. Families display ornamental dolls on tiered platforms and eat special foods like chirashi sushi and hina arare.

examples.japanese: {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}に{雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{飾|かざ}る。
examples.english: We display hina dolls for Girls' Day.

examples.japanese: {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}が{終|お}わったら{早|はや}めに{人形|にんぎょう}を{片付|かたづ}けないと{婚期|こんき}が{遅|おく}れると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that if you don't put the dolls away promptly after Girls' Day, marriage will be delayed.

examples.japanese: {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}は{三月三日|さんがつみっか}に{行|おこな}われ、{女|おんな}の{子|こ}の{健|すこ}やかな{成長|せいちょう}と{幸|しあわ}せを{願|ねが}う。
examples.english: The Peach Festival is held on March 3rd to pray for the healthy growth and happiness of girls.

notes:
CULTURE:
Also called ひな{祭|まつ}り (Doll Festival). One of the {五節句|ごせっく} (five seasonal festivals). The name comes from the peach blossoms ({桃|もも}の{花|はな}) that bloom around this time. Families with daughters display elaborate tiered platforms ({雛壇|ひなだん}) with ornamental dolls representing the imperial court. Traditional foods include {菱餅|ひしもち} (diamond-shaped rice cakes), {雛|ひな}あられ (bite-sized rice crackers), and {甘酒|あまざけ} or {白酒|しろざけ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}を{祝|いわ}う (to celebrate Girls' Day)
- {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}の{飾|かざ}り (Girls' Day decorations)
- {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}にちなんだ{和菓子|わがし} (Japanese sweets for Girls' Day)
